passages: Letter Published: 20 April 2016 Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage Alexis C.

Here we report the development of ‘base editing’, a new approach to genome editing that enables the direct, irreversible conversion of one target DNA base into another in a programmable manner, without requiring dsDNA backbone cleavage or a donor template.
Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage.
High-throughput profiling of off-target DNA cleavage reveals RNA-programmed Cas9 nuclease specificity.
Three days after plasmid delivery, genomic DNA was extracted and analysed for base editing at the six genomic loci by HTS.
